primary.english: Saving means keeping some money for later instead of spending it all now.
primary.sesotho: Ho boloka ho bolela ho boloka chelete bakeng sa hamorao.

primary.english: When you save, you put money away so you can use it another day.
primary.sesotho: Ha u boloka, u beha chelete ka thoko hore u e sebelise ka letsatsi le leng.

primary.english: Saving is like keeping a seed instead of eating it — you keep it for the future.
primary.sesotho: Ho boloka ho tshwana le ho boloka peo ho e-na le ho e ja.

primary.english: Saving means you do not spend all your money today.
primary.sesotho: Ho boloka ho bolela hore ha o sebedise chelete yohle kajeno.

primary.english: Saving is when you put money in a safe place and do not touch it.
primary.sesotho: Ho boloka ke ha o beha chelete sebakeng se sireletsehileng.

high_school.english: Saving is setting aside a portion of your income for future use.
high_school.sesotho: Ho boloka ke ho behella karolo ya moputso wa hao ka thoko.

high_school.english: Saving means deliberately keeping some money for later needs.
high_school.sesotho: Ho boloka ho bolela ho boloka chelete ka boomo bakeng sa ditlhoko tsa hamorao.

high_school.english: Saving is the habit of putting money aside regularly.
high_school.sesotho: Ho boloka ke tlwaelo ya ho behella chelete ka thoko kgafetsa.

high_school.english: When you save, you delay spending today so you have money tomorrow.
high_school.sesotho: Ha o boloka, o liehisa tshebediso kajeno hore o be le chelete hosane.

high_school.english: Saving is the foundation of financial health.
high_school.sesotho: Ho boloka ke motheo wa bophelo bo botle ba lichelete.

university.english: Saving is the deliberate allocation of income toward future goals.
university.sesotho: Ho boloka ke ho arola moputso ka boomo ho ya dipakaneng tsa bokamoso.

university.english: Saving means prioritizing financial security over immediate spending.
university.sesotho: Ho boloka ho bolela ho beha tshireletso ya lichelete pele.

university.english: Saving is a financial discipline providing liquidity for emergencies.
university.sesotho: Ho boloka ke taeo ya lichelete e fanang ka chelete ya tshohanyetso.

university.english: Saving involves allocating a percentage of income to build reserves.
university.sesotho: Ho boloka ho kenyelletsa ho arola peresente ya moputso ho haha pokello.

university.english: Saving builds financial assets through regular contributions.
university.sesotho: Ho boloka ho haha matlotlo a lichelete ka ho kenya chelete kgafetsa.

primary.english: If you get M10 and keep M3 for later, you saved M3.
primary.sesotho: Haeba o fumana M10 mme o boloka M3, o bolokile M3.

primary.english: Your grandmother gives you M5. You put M2 in your piggy bank.
primary.sesotho: Nkhono o fa M5. O kenya M2 ka piggy bank.

primary.english: A toy costs M50. Saving M10 per week means you will have it in 5 weeks.
primary.sesotho: Sebapadiswa se bitsa M50. Ho boloka M10 ka beke ho bolela hore o tla ba le sona ka dibeke tse 5.

primary.english: Instead of spending all your M20, you keep M5.
primary.sesotho: Ho e-na le ho sebedisa M20 yohle, o boloka M5.

primary.english: You have M100 and keep M30 for later.
primary.sesotho: O na le M100 mme o boloka M30 bakeng sa hamorao.

high_school.english: You earn M500 and save M100 monthly. After one year, you have M1,200.
high_school.sesotho: O fumana M500 mme o boloka M100 ka kgwedi. Kamora selemo, o na le M1,200.

high_school.english: Your allowance is M300. Set aside M50 before spending anything.
high_school.sesotho: Chelete ya hao ke M300. Behella M50 ka thoko pele o sebedisa letho.

high_school.english: You need M2,000 for a laptop. Saving M200 monthly means 10 months.
high_school.sesotho: O hloka M2,000 bakeng sa laptop. Ho boloka M200 ka kgwedi ho bolela dikgwedi tse 10.

high_school.english: Keep M50 from M200 instead of spending it all.
high_school.sesotho: Boloka M50 ho tswa ho M200 ho e-na le ho e sebedisa yohle.

high_school.english: A M1,000 gift: save 30 percent (M300) and spend the rest.
high_school.sesotho: Mpho ya M1,000: boloka 30% (M300) mme o sebedise tse setseng.

university.english: Bursary M2,500: follow 50/30/20 rule, save M500 monthly.
university.sesotho: Bursary ya M2,500: latela molao wa 50/30/20, boloka M500 ka kgwedi.

university.english: Freelance income M1,500: allocate M300 to savings first.
university.sesotho: Moputso wa freelance M1,500: arola M300 polokong pele.

university.english: Save M200 monthly for emergency fund = M2,400 per year.
university.sesotho: Boloka M200 ka kgwedi bakeng sa tshohanyetso = M2,400 ka selemo.

university.english: Invest M500 monthly at 7 percent = approximately M87,000 in 10 years.
university.sesotho: Kenya M500 ka kgwedi ka 7% = M87,000 ka dilemo tse 10.

university.english: Income M3,500: M2,000 fixed, M500 savings, M1,000 variable.
university.sesotho: Moputso M3,500: M2,000 e sa fetoheng, M500 poloko, M1,000 e fetohang.

primary.english: You need lots of money to save — FALSE! Even M1 counts.
primary.sesotho: O hloka chelete e ngata ho boloka — HA SE NNETE! Le M1 e a balwa.

primary.english: Saving is only for rich people — FALSE! Everyone can save.
primary.sesotho: Ho boloka ke ha barui feela — HA SE NNETE! Bohle ba ka boloka.

primary.english: Saving means no fun — FALSE! You can save and spend wisely.
primary.sesotho: Ho boloka ho bolela ho se thabe — HA SE NNETE! O ka boloka le ho sebedisa ka bohlale.

high_school.english: Only people with jobs can save — FALSE! Students can too.
high_school.sesotho: Ke batho ba nang le mesebetsi feela ba ka bolokang — HA SE NNETE! Baithuti le bona ba ka boloka.

high_school.english: You need M100+ to start — FALSE! M10 regularly adds up.
high_school.sesotho: O hloka M100+ ho qala — HA SE NNETE! M10 kgafetsa ea eketswa.

high_school.english: Saving means never spending on yourself — FALSE! It means balance.
high_school.sesotho: Ho boloka ho bolela ho se ithekele letho — HA SE NNETE! Ho bolela ho lekalekanya.

university.english: Saving equals investing — FALSE! Different risk levels.
university.sesotho: Ho boloka ho tshwana le matsete — HA SE NNETE! Di na le dikotsi tse fapaneng.

university.english: Save what is left after spending — FALSE! Pay yourself first.
university.sesotho: Boloka se setseng kamora ho sebedisa — HA SE NNETE! Itefe pele.

university.english: Inflation makes saving pointless — FALSE! Interest offsets it.
university.sesotho: Inflation e etsa hore ho boloka ho se thuse — HA SE NNETE! Phaello ea e lekanya.

follow_up_suggestions.english: Would you like to learn how to start saving?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o ka rata ho ithuta ho qala ho boloka?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Do you know what a piggy bank is?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o tseba hore na piggy bank ke eng?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Want to learn about saving goals?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o batla ho ithuta ka dipakane tsa poloko?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Would you like to know where to keep savings?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o ka rata ho tseba moo o bolokang poloko?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Should we talk about budgeting too?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na re bue le ka tekanyetso?

primary.english: Put money in a piggy bank every time you get some.
primary.sesotho: Kenya chelete ka piggy bank nako le nako ha o e fumana.

primary.english: Ask your parents to help you open a savings jar.
primary.sesotho: Kopa batswadi ho o thusa ho bula jar ya poloko.

primary.english: Start with M1 or M2. Even small amounts count!
primary.sesotho: Qala ka M1 kapa M2. Le tjhelete e nyane e a balwa!

high_school.english: Set a savings goal, then save a fixed amount each month.
high_school.sesotho: Beha pakane ya poloko, ebe o boloka tjhelete e behilweng kgwedi le kgwedi.

high_school.english: Open a bank savings account and deposit regularly.
high_school.sesotho: Bula akhaonto ya poloko bankeng mme o kene kgafetsa.

high_school.english: Use the 50/30/20 rule: save 20 percent of income.
high_school.sesotho: Sebedisa molao wa 50/30/20: boloka 20% ya moputso.

university.english: Automate your savings through a standing order.
university.sesotho: Etsa hore poloko e itsamaele ka standing order.

university.english: Build an emergency fund with 3-6 months of expenses.
university.sesotho: Haha letlole la tshohanyetso ka dikgwedi tse 3-6.

university.english: Track expenses and identify areas to reduce spending.
university.sesotho: Latela ditshenyehelo mme o bone moo o ka fokotsang.

primary.english: Saving helps you buy things you really want later.
primary.sesotho: Ho boloka ho o thusa ho reka dintho tseo o di batlang hamorao.

primary.english: Saving keeps your money safe for the future.
primary.sesotho: Ho boloka ho boloka chelete e sireletsehile bakeng sa bokamoso.

primary.english: When you save, you always have money for emergencies.
primary.sesotho: Ha o boloka, o dula o na le chelete ya tshohanyetso.

high_school.english: Saving builds financial security and peace of mind.
high_school.sesotho: Ho boloka ho haha tshireletso ya lichelete le kgotso.

high_school.english: Saving helps you achieve goals like buying a laptop.
high_school.sesotho: Ho boloka ho thusa ho fihlela dipakane tse kang ho reka laptop.

high_school.english: Saving prevents debt when unexpected expenses arise.
high_school.sesotho: Ho boloka ho thibela sekoloto ha ditshenyehelo tse sa lebellwang di hlaha.

university.english: Saving provides capital for investments and wealth building.
university.sesotho: Ho boloka ho fana ka motheo wa matsete le ho haha maruo.

university.english: An emergency fund prevents financial crises.
university.sesotho: Letlole la tshohanyetso le thibela mathata a lichelete.

university.english: Saving creates financial independence and options.
university.sesotho: Ho boloka ho bopa boikemelo ba lichelete le dikgetho.

situation.english: Mpho gets M20 pocket money. She wants to buy sweets (M5) and a toy (M15). Should she spend all or save some?
situation.sesotho: Mpho o fumana M20 ya pokotho. O batla ho reka dipompong (M5) le sebapadiswa (M15). Na o lokela ho sebedisa tsohle kapa ho boloka tse ding?

advice.english: Mpho should save at least M5. She can buy sweets and save the rest for the toy later.
advice.sesotho: Mpho o lokela ho boloka M5. A ka reka dipompong mme a boloke tse setseng bakeng sa sebapadiswa.

lesson.english: Always save something from what you receive.
lesson.sesotho: Dula o boloka ho hong ho tswa ho seo o se fumanang.

situation.english: Thabo wants a bicycle that costs M500. He gets M50 pocket money every week. How can he save for it?
situation.sesotho: Thabo o batla baesekele e bitsang M500. O fumana M50 ka beke. A ka e bolokela jwang?

advice.english: If Thabo saves M25 per week, he will have M500 in 20 weeks (5 months).
advice.sesotho: Haeba Thabo a boloka M25 ka beke, o tla ba le M500 ka dibeke tse 20 (dikgwedi tse 5).

lesson.english: Break big goals into smaller weekly savings.
lesson.sesotho: Arola dipakane tse kgolo ka dipoloko tse nyane tsa beke.

situation.english: Lerato earns M600 monthly from part-time work. She spends everything on entertainment. What should she change?
situation.sesotho: Lerato o fumana M600 ka kgwedi mosebetsing wa nakwana. O sebedisa tsohle boithabisong. O lokela ho fetola eng?

advice.english: Lerato should save at least M120 (20%). She can still enjoy M480 for other things.
advice.sesotho: Lerato o lokela ho boloka M120 (20%). A ka ntsha M480 bakeng sa dintho tse ding.

lesson.english: Pay yourself first before spending on wants.
lesson.sesotho: Itefe pele pele o sebedisa ditakatso.

situation.english: A student gets a M1,000 gift. They want to buy a new phone (M800) and go out with friends (M200). Is this wise?
situation.sesotho: Moithuti o fumana mpho ya M1,000. O batla ho reka fono (M800) le ho ya le metswalle (M200). Na see se bohlale?

advice.english: Better plan: Save M300, spend M500 on phone, M200 for friends. Or save M500 and buy a cheaper phone.
advice.sesotho: Leano le betere: Boloka M300, sebedisa M500 fonong, M200 metswalle. Kapa boloka M500 mme o reke fono e theko e tlase.

lesson.english: Balance saving and spending, even with gift money.
lesson.sesotho: Lekalekanya ho boloka le ho sebedisa, le ka chelete ya dimpho.

situation.english: A student receives M2,500 bursary monthly. Rent is M1,000, food M800, transport M300. How much should they save?
situation.sesotho: Moithuti o fumana bursary ya M2,500. Rente M1,000, dijo M800, dipalangwang M300. O lokela ho boloka bokae?

advice.english: After expenses: M400 remains. Save M300 and keep M100 for emergencies.
advice.sesotho: Kamora ditshenyehelo: M400 e setseng. Boloka M300 mme o boloke M100 bakeng sa tshohanyetso.

lesson.english: Always allocate surplus to savings before discretionary spending.
lesson.sesotho: Dula o arola se setseng polokong pele o sebedisa.

situation.english: A student has no savings and their laptop breaks. They need M3,000 urgently. What went wrong?
situation.sesotho: Moithuti ha a na poloko mme laptop ya hae e senyeha. O hloka M3,000 ka potlako. Ho senyehile eng?

advice.english: Without an emergency fund, unexpected expenses cause debt. Aim to save 3-6 months of expenses.
advice.sesotho: Ntle le letlole la tshohanyetso, ditshenyehelo tse sa lebellwang di baka sekoloto. Boloka dikgwedi tse 3-6 tsa ditshenyehelo.

lesson.english: Emergency funds prevent financial crises.
lesson.sesotho: Matlole a tshohanyetso a thibela mathata.

primary.english: Money is what we use to buy things. In Lesotho, we use Maloti and Lisente.
primary.sesotho: Chelete ke seo re se sebedisang ho reka dintho. Lesotho re sebedisa Maloti le Lisente.

primary.english: Money is special paper and coins that people use to pay for things.
primary.sesotho: Chelete ke pampiri le ditjhepe tse kgethehileng tseo batho ba di sebedisang ho lefa.

primary.english: Money helps us buy food, clothes, and other things we need.
primary.sesotho: Chelete e re thusa ho reka dijo, diaparo le dintho tse ding tseo re di hlokang.

primary.english: In Lesotho, our money is called the Loti.
primary.sesotho: Lesotho, chelete ya rona e bitswa Loti.

primary.english: Money is a tool for buying and selling things.
primary.sesotho: Chelete ke sesebediswa sa ho reka le ho rekisa.

high_school.english: Money is a medium of exchange used to buy goods and services.
high_school.sesotho: Chelete ke mokgwa wa ho fapanyetsana o sebediswang ho reka thepa le ditshebeletso.

high_school.english: The Loti is divided into 100 Lisente.
high_school.sesotho: Loti e arotswe ka Lisente tse 100.

high_school.english: Money has three functions: medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value.
high_school.sesotho: Chelete e na le mesebetsi e meraro: ho fapanyetsana, ho metha boleng le ho boloka boleng.

high_school.english: The Loti is pegged to the South African Rand.
high_school.sesotho: Loti e hokahane le Rand ya Afrika Borwa.

high_school.english: Money represents purchasing power.
high_school.sesotho: Chelete e emela matla a ho reka.

university.english: Money serves as medium of exchange, store of value, and unit of account.
university.sesotho: Chelete e sebetsa e le mokgwa wa ho fapanyetsana, ho boloka boleng le ho metha boleng.

university.english: The Lesotho Loti (LSL) is pegged 1:1 to the Rand (ZAR).
university.sesotho: Loti ya Lesotho (LSL) e hokahane 1:1 le Rand (ZAR).

university.english: Money encompasses M0 through M3 with implications for liquidity.
university.sesotho: Chelete e kenyelletsa M0 ho ya M3 ka ditlamorao tsa liquidity.

university.english: Understanding money requires analyzing banking and monetary policy.
university.sesotho: Ho utlwisisa chelete ho hloka ho hlahloba dibanka le leano la lichelete.

university.english: Digital money represents a new form of financial inclusion.
university.sesotho: Chelete ya dijithale e emela mokgwa o motjha wa ho kenyelletsa batho ditabeng tsa lichelete.

primary.english: A bread costs M10. You give M10 and get bread.
primary.sesotho: Bohobe bo bitsa M10. O fana ka M10 mme o fumana bohobe.

primary.english: M1 is the same as 100 Lisente.
primary.sesotho: M1 e tshwana le Lisente tse 100.

primary.english: A sweet costs M5. A packet of chips costs M10.
primary.sesotho: Pompong e bitsa M5. Pakete ya chips e bitsa M10.

primary.english: M50 can buy five breads that cost M10 each.
primary.sesotho: M50 e ka reka mahobe a mahlano a bitsang M10 ka bonngwe.

primary.english: You have M20 and want to buy something that costs M15. You have M5 left.
primary.sesotho: O na le M20 mme o batla ho reka ntho e bitsang M15. O setse le M5.

high_school.english: M50 can be exchanged for goods worth M50.
high_school.sesotho: M50 e ka fapanyetswa ka thepa ya boleng ba M50.

high_school.english: At 5 percent inflation, M100 today buys only M95 worth next year.
high_school.sesotho: Ka inflation ya 5%, M100 kajeno e reka feela M95 selemong se tlang.

high_school.english: M1 equals R1 because of the peg.
high_school.sesotho: M1 e lekana le R1 ka lebaka la peg.

high_school.english: Counting money: M20 + M10 + M5 = M35.
high_school.sesotho: Ho bala chelete: M20 + M10 + M5 = M35.

high_school.english: You receive M500 and can spend or save it.
high_school.sesotho: O fumana M500 mme o ka e sebedisa kapa ho e boloka.

university.english: The Loti-Rand peg means shared monetary policy with South Africa.
university.sesotho: Peg ya Loti le Rand e bolela leano le kopaneng la lichelete le Afrika Borwa.

university.english: M1,000 in cash has different implications than M1,000 in savings.
university.sesotho: M1,000 ya cash e na le moelelo o fapaneng le M1,000 polokong.

university.english: Depositing M500 enters the broader money supply.
university.sesotho: Ho kenya M500 ho kena ka hara pokello e pharaletseng ya chelete.

university.english: Purchasing power parity compares prices between Maseru and Bloemfontein.
university.sesotho: Purchasing power parity e bapisa ditheko pakeng tsa Maseru le Bloemfontein.

university.english: Mobile money like M-Pesa affects financial inclusion.
university.sesotho: Mobile money e kang M-Pesa e ama ho kenyelletswa ditabeng tsa lichelete.

primary.english: Money grows on trees — FALSE! People earn money by working.
primary.sesotho: Chelete e mela difateng — HA SE NNETE! Batho ba fumana chelete ka ho sebetsa.

primary.english: More money means more happiness — FALSE! Money helps but is not everything.
primary.sesotho: Chelete e ngata e bolela thabo e ngata — HA SE NNETE! Chelete ea thusa empa ha se yohle.

primary.english: Only adults use money — FALSE! Children can learn to use money too.
primary.sesotho: Ke batho ba baholo feela ba sebedisang chelete — HA SE NNETE! Bana le bona ba ka ithuta.

high_school.english: Debit cards are unlimited money — FALSE! They only access your account.
high_school.sesotho: Dikarete tsa debit ke chelete e sa feleng — HA SE NNETE! Di fihlella feela akhaonto ya hao.

high_school.english: The Loti and Rand are the same currency — FALSE! Different but pegged.
high_school.sesotho: Loti le Rand ke chelete e le nngwe — HA SE NNETE! Di fapane empa di hokahane.

high_school.english: Banks print money — FALSE! The Central Bank controls money supply.
high_school.sesotho: Dibanka di hatisa chelete — HA SE NNETE! Banka e Kgolo e laola tlhahiso ya chelete.

university.english: Cryptocurrency is legal tender in Lesotho — FALSE!
university.sesotho: Cryptocurrency ke chelete ya molao Lesotho — HA SE NNETE!

university.english: Money has intrinsic value — FALSE! Fiat money has value by decree.
university.sesotho: Chelete e na le boleng ba tlhaho — HA SE NNETE! Fiat money e na le boleng ka molao.

university.english: Inflation always hurts everyone — FALSE! Borrowers with fixed rates benefit.
university.sesotho: Inflation e utlwisa bohle bohloko — HA SE NNETE! Ba alimang ka fixed rates ba a rua molemo.

follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o batla ho ithuta ho bala Maloti?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Would you like to know where money comes from?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o ka rata ho tseba moo chelete e tswang teng?

follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na re bue ka ho boloka chelete?

follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o batla ho utlwisisa hore na dibanka di etsa eng ka chelete?

follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o ka rata ho ithuta ka ho fumana chelete?

primary.english: Count your coins and notes to know how much you have.
primary.sesotho: Bala ditjhepe le dipampiri ho tseba hore na o na le bokae.

primary.english: Learn that M1 equals 100 Lisente.
primary.sesotho: Ithute hore M1 e lekana le Lisente tse 100.

primary.english: Practice buying small things to understand prices.
primary.sesotho: Ikwetlise ho reka dintho tse nyane ho utlwisisa ditheko.

high_school.english: Understand that the Loti is pegged to the Rand.
high_school.sesotho: Utlwisisa hore Loti e hokahane le Rand.

high_school.english: Track how much money comes in and goes out.
high_school.sesotho: Latela chelete e kenang le e tswang.

high_school.english: Learn about inflation and purchasing power.
high_school.sesotho: Ithute ka inflation le matla a ho reka.

university.english: Understand monetary policy and the Common Monetary Area.
university.sesotho: Utlwisisa leano la lichelete le Common Monetary Area.

university.english: Analyze how digital money affects financial inclusion.
university.sesotho: Hlahloba kamoo chelete ya dijithale e amang ho kenyelletswa.

university.english: Study the money multiplier and fractional reserve banking.
university.sesotho: Ithute ka money multiplier le fractional reserve banking.

primary.english: We need money to buy food, clothes, and other things.
primary.sesotho: Re hloka chelete ho reka dijo, diaparo le dintho tse ding.

primary.english: Money helps us trade fairly.
primary.sesotho: Chelete e re thusa ho rekisana ka toka.

primary.english: Understanding money helps you make good choices.
primary.sesotho: Ho utlwisisa chelete ho thusa ho etsa dikgetho tse ntle.

high_school.english: Money makes trade efficient.
high_school.sesotho: Chelete e etsa kgwebo e be bonolo.

high_school.english: Understanding money helps you manage finances.
high_school.sesotho: Ho utlwisisa chelete ho thusa ho laola lichelete.

high_school.english: The Loti-Rand peg stabilizes the economy.
high_school.sesotho: Peg ya Loti le Rand e tsitsisa moruo.

university.english: Money serves as store of value and unit of account.
university.sesotho: Chelete e boloka boleng le ho metha boleng.

university.english: Monetary policy affects inflation and growth.
university.sesotho: Leano la lichelete le ama inflation le kgolo.

university.english: Digital money is transforming financial services.
university.sesotho: Chelete ya dijithale e fetola ditshebeletso.

situation.english: You have M50. A bread costs M10. How many breads can you buy?
situation.sesotho: O na le M50. Bohobe bo bitsa M10. O ka reka mahobe a makae?

advice.english: M50 divided by M10 = 5 breads. You can buy 5 breads.
advice.sesotho: M50 arolwa ka M10 = mahobe a 5. O ka reka mahobe a 5.

lesson.english: Division helps you know how many things you can buy.
lesson.sesotho: Ho arola ho o thusa ho tseba hore na o ka reka dintho tse kae.

situation.english: A sweet costs M2. You have M10. How many sweets can you buy?
situation.sesotho: Pompong e bitsa M2. O na le M10. O ka reka dipompong tse kae?

advice.english: M10 divided by M2 = 5 sweets.

lesson.english: Start with education before investing money.
lesson.sesotho: Qala ka thuto pele o kenya chelete.

primary.english: Saving is keeping money safe. Investing is using money to try to make more money.
primary.sesotho: Ho boloka ke ho boloka chelete e sireletsehile. Matsete ke ho sebedisa chelete ho leka ho etsa e ngata.

high_school.english: Saving has low risk but low returns. Investing has higher risk but potentially higher returns.
high_school.sesotho: Ho boloka ho na le kotsi e tlase empa phaello e tlase. Matsete a na le kotsi e kgolo empa phaello e ka ba kgolo.

university.english: Saving preserves capital with minimal risk (e.g., 3-5% interest). Investing deploys capital for growth (e.g., 7-12% returns) with market risk.
university.sesotho: Ho boloka ho boloka chelete ka kotsi e nyane (3-5%). Matsete a sebedisa chelete bakeng sa kgolo (7-12%) ka kotsi ya mmaraka.

primary.english: Needs are things you MUST have to live. Wants are things you would LIKE but can live without.
primary.sesotho: Ditlhoko ke tseo o T LAMEHANG ho ba le tsona. Ditakatso ke tseo o ka phelang ntle le tsona.

high_school.english: Needs are essential for survival and wellbeing. Wants improve quality of life but are optional.
high_school.sesotho: Ditlhoko di bohlokwa bakeng sa ho phela. Ditakatso di ntlafatsa bophelo empa ke tsa boikgethelo.

university.english: Needs are non-discretionary (rent, food, healthcare). Wants are discretionary (entertainment, luxury items).
university.sesotho: Ditlhoko ha di qojwe (rente, dijo). Ditakatso ke tsa boikgethelo (boithabiso).

primary.english: Simple interest is calculated once on your starting money. Compound interest is calculated on your money PLUS the interest you earned.
primary.sesotho: E bonolo e balwa hanngwe hodima chelete ya hao. E kopaneng e balwa hodima chelete LE phaello e fumanweng.

high_school.english: Simple interest: I = P x r x t (principal only). Compound interest: A = P(1+r)^n (principal + accumulated interest).
high_school.sesotho: E bonolo: I = P x r x t. E kopaneng: A = P(1+r)^n.

university.english: Simple interest grows linearly. Compound interest grows exponentially — this is why it accelerates wealth building.
university.sesotho: E bonolo e hola ka mokgwa o otlolohileng. E kopaneng e hola ka exponentially.

primary.english: A loan must be paid back. A gift is free and does not need to be returned.
primary.sesotho: Kalimo e tlameha ho kgutliswa. Mpho ke ya mahala mme ha e kgutliswe.

high_school.english: A loan is borrowed money with repayment obligation. A gift has no repayment requirement.
high_school.sesotho: Kalimo ke chelete e alimilweng e hlokang ho kgutliswa. Mpho ha e hloke ho kgutliswa.

university.english: Loans create debt obligations with interest. Gifts are transfers without reciprocal obligation.
university.sesotho: Dikoloto di bopa boitlamo le phaello. Dimpho ke phetiso ntle le boitlamo.

primary.english: A bank is a building where you keep money. Mobile money is on your phone.
primary.sesotho: Banka ke moaho moo o bolokang chelete. Mobile money e fonong ya hao.

high_school.english: Banks offer more services (loans, interest) but may have fees. Mobile money is convenient but has transfer fees.
high_school.sesotho: Dibanka di fana ka ditshebeletso tse ngata empa di lefisa. Mobile money e bonolo empa e na le ditefiso.

university.english: Banks are regulated financial institutions with deposit insurance. Mobile money operators are telecom-based with different regulations.
university.sesotho: Dibanka di laolwa ka molao. Mobile money e itshetlehile ho telecom.

primary.english: Income is money you receive. Profit is money left after paying costs.
primary.sesotho: Moputso ke chelete eo o e fumanang. Phaello ke chelete e setseng kamora ho lefa ditshenyehelo.

high_school.english: Income is total money received. Profit = Income - Expenses.
high_school.sesotho: Moputso ke kakaretso e fumanweng. Phaello = Moputso - Ditshenyehelo.

university.english: Income (revenue) is the top line. Profit is the bottom line after all costs, taxes, and expenses.
university.sesotho: Moputso ke top line. Phaello ke bottom line kamora ditshenyehelo tsohle.

situation.english: A student loses their bursary due to academic performance. They have M1,000 saved and monthly expenses of M1,500. What should they do?
situation.sesotho: Moithuti o lahlehetswe ke bursary. O na le M1,000 e bolokilweng le ditshenyehelo tsa M1,500 ka kgwedi. O etse eng?

advice.english: First, cut all non-essential spending. Find part-time work quickly. Apply for other funding. The M1,000 is a buffer for 2-3 weeks.
advice.sesotho: Pele, fokotsa tshebediso e sa hlokahaleng. Fumana mosebetsi wa nakwana. Kopa dithuso tse ding. M1,000 ke buffer ya dibeke tse 2-3.

lesson.english: Emergency funds buy you time during crises.
lesson.sesotho: Matlole a tshohanyetso a o reka nako mathateng.

situation.english: A friend asks to borrow M200 and promises to repay next month. You know they already owe others money. What should you do?
situation.sesotho: Motswalle o kopa M200 mme o tshepisa ho kgutlisa kgwedi e tlang. O tseba hore o se a kolota batho ba bang. O etse eng?

advice.english: Politely decline or lend only what you can afford to lose. Never lend money you need for your own expenses.
advice.sesotho: Hana ka mosa kapa alima feela seo o ka se lahlehelwang. O se ke wa alima chelete eo o e hlokang.

lesson.english: Protect your financial wellbeing, even with friends.
lesson.sesotho: Sireletsa bophelo ba hao ba lichelete, le ho metswalle.

situation.english: You spent M400 on entertainment and now have only M100 for food for two weeks. What went wrong and how do you fix it?
situation.sesotho: O sebedisitse M400 boithabisong mme o setse le M100 bakeng sa dijo dibeke tse pedi. Ho senyehile eng?

advice.english: You prioritized wants over needs. Fix: Buy basic food (rice, mealie meal). Avoid entertainment until next month.
advice.sesotho: O behile ditakatso pele ho ditlhoko. Fix: Reka dijo tsa motheo. Qoba boithabiso ho fihlela kgwedi e tlang.

lesson.english: Always budget for needs before spending on wants.
lesson.sesotho: Dula o rera ditlhoko pele o sebedisa ditakatso.

situation.english: Your phone breaks and you need it for school. Repairs cost M500 but you only have M200 saved.
situation.sesotho: Fono ya hao e senyehile mme o e hloka bakeng sa sekolo. Ho lokisa M500 empa o bolokile M200 feela.

advice.english: This is why emergency funds matter. Borrow M300 from family (interest-free) or find temporary work. Next time, save more.
advice.sesotho: Ke ka hona matlole a tshohanyetso a le bohlokwa. Alima M300 lelapeng kapa fumana mosebetsi wa nakwana.

lesson.english: Emergency funds should cover unexpected repairs.
lesson.sesotho: Matlole a tshohanyetso a lokela ho akaretsa ditokiso tse sa lebellwang.
